entries.body:
Okay. Dinner last night was really good. Annoyingly good, actually.

First, he was late. Twenty minutes. But he texted me, explained what was happening, and apologized when he got there. So I don't really have a complaint about the lateness itself. I appreciated that he told me.

And then he was just…really good company. We talked for hours. He remembered something I told him about a work situation and asked me how it turned out. I like that. I don't want to have to reintroduce myself every time I see someone.

He also challenged me on something we were talking about. Not in an obnoxious way. He actually made a good point. I really like how intelligent he is. And he's funny. And obviously I'm attracted to him. Very attracted to him.

His hands are also extremely nice. I know that's a ridiculous thing to say, but I have a criterion for this. I am allowed to have a preference.

He checked his phone once during dinner because something was happening at work. He explained it, apologized, and put it away. That didn't bother me much. I understand that his job is demanding. What bothers me is that sometimes I don't hear from him for most of the day, and then when we're together he's completely attentive.

I don't want to be unreasonable. I don't need a minute-by-minute update. But I also don't want a relationship where I only feel like I exist when I'm physically in the same room as him.

The good thing is that he actually made the next plan. I didn't have to bring it up or hint around it. He said we should do something next weekend, and made the reservation, again. He confirmed this morning.

I think he likes me. I just don't know whether the communication thing is a difference in style or something that will become a bigger problem. One amazing date doesn't change things or answer that question.

And I know I'm very attracted to him, and I unfortunately like him a lot. I need to make sure I'm not letting that make me too generous about things that actually matter to me or that I'm making excuses that shouldn't slide.
entries._comment: Same occurred_on as Adrian's adr-datenight: this is when the evening happened. She wrote it the next morning ('last night'), he wrote it that night ('tonight').

entries.body: Didn't hear from Adrian from Tuesday morning until Thursday night. He was in a production block, I know that. He surfaced Thursday with a long message and a plan for the weekend. I don't think he was avoiding me. I think I genuinely did not cross his mind for two days, which is somehow a different thing and I am not sure it is a better one.

observations.text: No contact from Tuesday morning to Thursday evening.
He initiated contact on Thursday with a plan for the weekend.
She reads the silence as absence of thought rather than avoidance.
Whether she has told him what frequency would feel like enough.
observations.hedge: You haven't mentioned discussing this with him directly — have you?

evidence.rationale: Two days without contact is the pattern she named as her concern.
A demanding production block is the career she said she wanted him to have.
The same fact reads as ambition and as unavailability; it does not resolve to either.

entries.body: Second date with Adrian. He is genuinely one of the most attractive men I have ever sat across a table from, which I had assumed would be the whole story, and then he turned out to be interesting. He asked what I actually do, not what my title is. I came home annoyed about how much I liked it.

observations.text: He asked about the substance of her work rather than her title.
She was unsettled by how much she enjoyed it.

evidence.rationale: One conversation is consistent with intellectual interest without establishing it.

entries.body: Third and last date with Joe. He is lovely to look at and extremely easy to be around and I ran out of things to say by the main course. He did not seem to notice, which was somehow the answer. Nothing was wrong. There just was not anything there.

observations.text: Conversation did not sustain across the evening.
She took his not noticing as confirmation rather than as a separate fact.

assessments.note: He communicates well when something changes. Between dates is the open question, and one good evening did not answer it.
He has said eventually. That is not nothing and it is not an answer.
The thing I actually need to find out.
Three evenings and I was doing all of the work.
